question: The All-India Muslim League adopted the Lahore Resolution in the year _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1940**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Lahore Resolution was adopted by the All-India Muslim League during its three-day general session held between 22nd and 24th March 1940.
 
• The resolution is also known as the Pakistan Resolution because it called for the creation of independent states for Muslims in the north-western and eastern zones of India.
 
• The resolution was presented by A. K. Fazlul Huq, the then Prime Minister of Bengal, and was supported by prominent leaders such as Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
 
• This resolution laid the foundation for the demand for Pakistan, which eventually led to the creation of the separate nation in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All-India Muslim League:**

 
 
• The All-India Muslim League was a political party in British India that played a crucial role in the creation of Pakistan.
 
• Founded in 1906 in Dhaka, the league initially sought to protect the rights of Muslims in India.
 
• Under the leadership of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the league adopted the demand for a separate Muslim state.
 
 
 
• **Lahore Resolution:**
 
 
• The Lahore Resolution, also known as the Pakistan Resolution, was a formal political statement adopted by the Muslim League in 1940.
 
• It called for the establishment of "independent states" in the north-western and eastern zones of India where Muslims were in the majority.
 
• This resolution is considered a significant step towards the creation of Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Ali Jinnah:**
 
 
• Muhammad Ali Jinnah was a prominent leader of the All-India Muslim League and played a pivotal role in the creation of Pakistan.
 
• He is also known as the "Father of the Nation" in Pakistan.
 
• Jinnah's leadership and advocacy for a separate Muslim state were instrumental in the partition of India in 1947.
